intro.title: Platform Detection Widget
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple widget that detects and displays the current platform your app is running on, such as iOS, Android, or the web. You'll learn how to use the Capacitor Platform API to access device information in a cross-platform way. The main technologies involved are Ionic for the UI, Angular for the component structure, and Capacitor for native platform detection. This is a beginner-friendly introduction to working with platform-specific features in a hybrid mobile app.
intro.usecase: Platform detection is essential in cross-platform mobile apps to deliver tailored experiences for iOS, Android, and web users. Real-world examples include apps like Spotify adjusting player controls for iOS gestures, banking apps showing biometric login options based on platform capabilities, and e-commerce apps optimizing checkout flows for mobile versus desktop. Developers use platform detection to conditionally load native plugins, apply platform-specific UI styling, or enable hardware features like camera or GPS that behave differently across devices. This pattern appears in settings panels that show device-specific options, onboarding flows that adapt to platform conventions, and analytics dashboards that track usage by operating system.
